families.title: Real positive-definite counterexamples to extended q-permanent monotonicity
families.kind: Counterexample and all-parameter extension
families.summary: For every real parameter q>1, a real symmetric positive-definite matrix has a negative q-permanent derivative at q. An explicit matrix of order five decreases from q=14 to q=15. Correlation matrices with no zero entries and integer-entry examples are also obtained. The dimension can depend on q. The real-symmetric question on [−1,1] remains outside the result.
families.source: Da Fonseca, 2010, Conjecture 1; 2018, Conjecture 2.

families.title: Gyires's permanent inequality for structured matrices
families.kind: Structured matrix inequalities and related polynomial bounds
families.summary: The preprint includes nonnegative circulants of orders five, six, and seven; all-order permutation polynomials aI+bQ+cQ²; all-order four-block matrices; one exceptional column or row; and all rank-at-most-two doubly stochastic matrices through order fifteen. It also proves structural, scalar, polynomial, deletion, balancing, local, and counting results. Exact counterexamples identify failed auxiliary assertions. The principal order-five and order-six claims, the all-order permutation-polynomial theorem, the all-order four-block theorem, and the exceptional-vector theorem have complete Lean proofs. General permanent comparisons and direct-sum closure also have Lean proofs. The rank-two result has a complete Lean proof for orders 2 through 8. The general order-seven circulant result and rank-two orders 9 through 15 remain incomplete in Lean. The unrestricted conjecture remains outside these results.
families.source: Gyires, 1978; Cheon and Wanless, 2005, Conjecture 20. Earlier formalization at the pinned Gyires repository.
families.formal_scope: The selected Comparator statements cover order-five circulants, the all-order four-block theorem, and the exceptional-vector theorem for n ≥ 2. Separate Lean packages prove the general order-six and all-order permutation-polynomial theorems. General permanent comparisons and direct-sum closure are also proved in Lean. The rank-two theorem has a complete Lean proof for orders 2 through 8. The general order-seven circulant theorem and rank-two orders 9 through 15 remain incomplete in Lean.

families.title: A polygon enclosure fails for sums of normal matrices
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
keywords: determinants of sums of normal matrices
families.summary: A polygon enclosure fails for a specified pair of normal matrices and its complete transposition graph.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified. Professor Kovačec found a counterexample to his conjecture in June 2026, documented in an unpublished preprint, and Wenlin Zhang sent him another; equivalence with this construction has not been established. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.
families.formal_scope: Actual normal matrices, determinants, straight-segment exterior and component exclusion are formalized. Correspondence with an external source conjecture is conditional.

families.title: An unbounded obstruction to projection AM–GM in Loewner order
families.kind: Focused research note and reproducible proof package
families.summary: Three rank-one orthogonal projections in dimension three violate the symmetrized-product Loewner AM–GM bound. No finite real multiplier repairs it, even with a positive-definite mean. The examples do not satisfy the additional nonsingular block structure of the motivating coordinate-descent application.
families.source: The manuscript credits the motivating Sun–Luo–Ye projection comparison and distinguishes nearby norm inequalities. Exact correspondence with the published conjecture and historical priority remain conditional.
families.formal_scope: Lean verifies a rational three-projection matrix obstruction and a parameterized obstruction for every real multiplier in dimension three; rank-one, positive-definite mean, rational all-multiplier choices, and the standard minimal-factor observation have complete conventional proofs.

families.title: An entropy increase for a structurally disassortative DomiRank graph
families.kind: Counterexample to an interval monotonicity conjecture
families.summary: A connected graph with 14 vertices and 32 edges has negative degree–log-degree edge covariance. All resolvent scores are positive on [251/1000,63/250] inside the stable domain. Its entropy nevertheless increases by more than 1/10000 in natural-logarithm units. This refutes the source’s assertion for every positive-score interval.
families.source: Zhang and Zhao, arXiv:2610.00107v4, Conjecture 4.9.

families.title: Ultra-log-concavity of domination sequences of powers of paths and cycles
families.kind: Ultra-log-concavity of domination sequences
families.summary: The domination counts of every natural power of a path or cycle form an ultra-log-concave sequence. The proof includes all natural graph orders and powers, the binomial normalization, and the boundary graph cases.
families.source: Galvin and Zhang, Conjecture 1.8.
families.formal_scope: Actual finite graph domination counts for powers of paths and cycles. No theorem for arbitrary graphs or real-rootedness is asserted.

families.title: Sharp escape of complex domination roots in square flowers
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: Sharp complex-root escape for square flowers, with complete flower and book real-root classifications and multiplicities.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: All numbered manuscript conclusions are formalized in seventy modules with 258 endpoint audits. Historical novelty and exact external-source correspondence remain provisional.

families.title: Leaf deletion can move the unique mode of a tree domination polynomial by two
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: Deleting a leaf can move the unique mode of an explicit tree domination polynomial by two.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The fixed tree, deletion, actual domination counts and unique-mode movement are formalized. External question identity and historical priority remain provisional.

families.title: Diagonal concavity does not imply concavity for sums of elementary symmetric polynomials
families.kind: Counterexample and complete parameter classification
families.summary: For positive M, let f=1+Mσ₁+σ₂+Mσ₃+σ₄ in four variables. Its fourth root is concave on the positive diagonal exactly when M≥1. It is concave on the full positive orthant exactly when M=1. Every M>1 therefore disproves Lachaume’s diagonal criterion with strictly positive coefficients.
families.source: Lachaume, arXiv:1712.10327v1, Conjecture 1.

families.title: Sharp root log-concavity of alternating Motzkin sums
families.kind: Conjecture resolution with an optimal threshold
families.summary: Let Tₙ be the alternating sum of Motzkin numbers through index n. The sequence Tₙ^(1/n) is strictly log-concave on its tail starting at five. The inequality reverses at center five, so no earlier tail is log-concave. This strengthens Zhao’s proposed tail starting at nine. The source recurrence and finite sum are linked in Lean.
families.source: Zhao, INTEGERS 26 (2026), A55, Conjecture 1; OEIS A187306.

families.title: Sharp log-concavity for alternating Motzkin sums
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: A robust bounded-forcing recurrence theorem and corrected scaled corollary, with applications to alternating Motzkin-type sums.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The arbitrary-real recurrence theorem and scaled corollary, including zero forcing, are formalized. Concrete sequences, uniform-family applications, root transfer and threshold classification retain conventional proofs.

families.title: Counterexamples to a late-iterate ordering conjecture for generalized Hofstadter functions
families.kind: Counterexamples for every parameter k≥4
families.summary: For every k≥4, some input n satisfies Fₖ^(2k+1)(n)>Fₖ₊₁^(2k+2)(n). The proof constructs inverse iterates whose exact gap is k−3. The finite witness F₄⁹(132)=8>7=F₅¹⁰(132) gives the first instance. The result concerns infinitely many parameters, not infinitely many violating inputs for each fixed parameter.
families.source: Letouzey, Li, and Steiner, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), 26.3.3, conjecture before Lemma 7.6.

families.title: A positive constant-recursive sequence with nonquasipolynomial power ranks
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: Exact minimal recurrences for every power of a rank-thirteen sequence, nonquasipolynomial ranks, and infinitely many power-rank profiles at each rank at least three.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified. Eric Rowland has independently obtained an infinite family of rank sequences for rank-three recurrences; the constructions have not been compared. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.
families.formal_scope: The main and arbitrary-rank companion theorems are formalized. Generating-function and polynomial corollaries retain conventional proofs.

families.title: The sharp level-one Fourier weight at density one eighth
families.kind: Sharp finite-cube Fourier bound
families.summary: For every Boolean indicator of mean 1/8 on a finite uniform cube, the level-one Fourier weight is at most 3/64. A codimension-three subcube attains the bound in every dimension at least three.
families.source: Yu, On Average Distance, Level-1 Fourier Weight, and Chang’s Lemma, 2026 revision. Yijia Fang and Hao Huang proved this bound earlier, with the equality cases (arXiv:2610.40486, 29 October 2026; circulated privately about a month before); I make no originality or priority claim. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.
families.formal_scope: The formal proof includes arbitrary dimensions, the exact moment identities, the Hamming-distance bound, and sharpness witnesses.

families.title: A quartic entropy deficit for random rankings
families.kind: Entropy deficit from pairwise comparison bias
families.summary: A distribution on rankings of n labels has entropy at most (1 − ε⁴/144) log(n!) if every pairwise comparison has probability at distance at least ε > 0 from 1/2.
families.source: Acan, Devlin, and Kahn, 2019; the manuscript identifies the established entropy arguments.
families.formal_scope: The proof includes all finite sizes and actual position-valued permutations. It assumes neither independent comparisons nor transitive preferred directions.

families.title: Sharp universal Rényi threshold for iid sums on finite Sidon sets
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: A sharp universal Renyi-order threshold for iid sums supported on finite strong-B2 sets.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The finite-support iid theorem, zero probabilities and critical endpoint are formalized. Comparison with unverified source definitions is conditional.

families.title: A 64-point spectral tile in F₂⁹ with no periodic complement
families.kind: Explicit counterexample, classification of complements and reproducible proof package
families.summary: An explicit 64-point subset E of F₂⁹, built from eight three-dimensional subspaces of F₂⁶ in the fibres over F₂³, is spectral with spectrum C × F₂³ and tiles F₂⁹ with the complement T = C × {0}, where C is an affine eight-circuit. Every tiling complement of E is a translate of T, and none is periodic, so no linear subspace complements E and F₂⁹ fails the periodic tiling property. This answers negatively the subspace-complement part of a question of Ferguson and Iosevich; whether every spectral 64-point subset of F₂⁹ tiles remains open.
families.formal_scope: Spectrality with an actual basis of all complex functions on E, the tiling E ⊕ T = F₂⁹, aperiodicity of E, the exclusion of every periodic and every subspace complement, the classification of all complements as the 512 translates of T, and the failure of the periodic tiling property for F₂⁹ are formalized in 16 Lean modules. Minimality of dimension nine depends on an external dimension-eight theorem and is not formalized.
families.source: Ferguson and Iosevich (arXiv:2610.36417, October 2026) asked whether spectral 64-point subsets of F₂⁹ have subspace tiling complements; Fan and Zhang defined the periodic tiling property for finite abelian groups. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified. Ferguson and Iosevich were already aware of counterexamples to the stronger statement; equivalence with this construction has not been established, and an AI-generated comparison suggesting non-equivalence is unverified. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.

families.title: The small-coefficient upper half of the Keller–Klein conjecture
families.kind: Theorem completing an open range and reproducible proof package
families.summary: For X = Σ vᵢεᵢ with independent uniform signs, Σ vᵢ² = 1 and |vᵢ| ≤ a ≤ 7/100, P(|X| ≤ x) ≤ 2Φ(x) + 2Φ(a) − 2 for every x ≥ 0, equivalently P(X ≤ x) − Φ(x) ≤ Φ(a) − 1/2. This is the upper half of the Keller–Klein conjecture in the small-coefficient range that Ivanisvili's computer-assisted manuscript of 21 October 2026 leaves open; with his results it implies the full conjecture, conditionally on those unrefereed external results.
families.formal_scope: The theorem for every finite vector of real coefficients, with the exact count of sign vectors and Mathlib's standard normal distribution function, is formalized in 62 Lean modules, including Prawitz smoothing, the characteristic-function envelopes and both analytic zones. Ivanisvili's Theorems 1.1 and 10.9, needed for the full conjecture, are external computer-assisted results and are not formalized.
families.source: Keller and Klein stated the conjecture in their proof of Tomaszewski's conjecture (Adv. Math. 2022, Conjecture 9.3). Ivanisvili (21 October 2026) proved the lower half and the case a ≥ 0.07 and proposed the analytic route used here. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: The exact asymmetric Merino–Welsh region for finite matroids
families.kind: Exact asymmetric parameter region
families.summary: The theorem characterizes all nonnegative pairs (x,y) for which T_M(x,0) T_M(0,y) ≥ T_M(1,1)² holds for every finite matroid without loops or coloops.
families.source: Liu, 2026; Chen and Xie, 2026. The manuscript states the relation to the diagonal theorem.
families.formal_scope: The statement uses actual Mathlib matroids and the literal subset rank sum. It includes empty ground sets and finite ground sets in arbitrary ambient types.

families.title: A rational five-cycle for two-block ADMM with multiplier step below two
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: An exact period-five orbit for multiplier-only two-block ADMM at step 199/100.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: Seven modules and eleven endpoint audits cover the orbit, minimizers and optimizer. Analytic regularity of the finite strongly convex extension retains a conventional proof.

families.title: A narrow interval for the universal multiplier step of two-block ADMM
families.kind: Convergence theorem, periodic counterexample and reproducible proof package
families.summary: Two-block ADMM with relaxation only in the multiplier update converges for every constant step 0 < τ ≤ 943/500 = 1.886 on finite-dimensional convex problems whose proximal subproblems attain their minima and which have a saddle point; both primal blocks, the multiplier and the objective values converge. Fixed compact polytopes in R^128 with zero objectives have a nonconstant periodic orbit for every τ ≥ 897744153596994489/475778439151265168 ≈ 1.8868954. The largest step with universal convergence therefore lies in an interval of width below 0.0009; its exact value is open.
families.formal_scope: The consensus convergence theorem for 0 < τ ≤ 943/500, the arbitrary-rank and full-rank affine-constraint theorems, both finite-memory certificates and the periodic orbit in R^128 are formalized in 168 Lean modules. Individual objective-value limits, the reduction from proper closed convex functions to proximal attainment, and penalty rescaling are conventional.
families.source: Fortin and Glowinski proved convergence for steps below the golden ratio; Tao and Yuan call the general convex case Glowinski's open question. Gao et al. (2022) asserted the range 1 < τ ≤ 2, which the periodic orbit contradicts. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Escaping Nesterov flows and iterates below critical damping
families.kind: Sharp thresholds, explicit counterexamples and reproducible proof package
families.summary: For the Nesterov differential equation X″ + (r/t)X′ + ∇F(X) = 0 from rest, and for the Nesterov iteration with momentum k/(k+r), universal boundedness over convex objectives with 1-Lipschitz gradient and attained minimum holds on the Hilbert space ℓ²(ℕ;ℝ²) exactly when r ≥ 3. The explicit planar potential h(√(x²+y²)) − x, with the Huber function h, has an escaping trajectory from (2,1) for every 0 < r ≤ 2 and bounded trajectories for r > 2. The finite-dimensional range 2 < r < 3 is open.
families.formal_scope: The continuous-time Hilbert-space threshold, the discrete threshold and the planar escape for 1 < r ≤ 2, including actual gradients, global solutions from rest and norm divergence, are formalized. The planar escape of the same potential for 0 < r ≤ 1, its boundedness for r > 2 and existence of solutions for r ≤ 1 are conventional.
families.source: Su, Boyd and Candès introduced the equation; boundedness for r ≥ 3 is classical, and Jang and Ryu record the subcritical case as open. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Periodic obstructions to small-extrapolation Chambolle–Pock
families.kind: Counterexample families, exact threshold and reproducible proof package
families.summary: For the unmodified Chambolle–Pock method, every step product κ = τσ‖L‖² > 2 admits fixed compact polytopes in R^4 whose iteration is periodic and nonconvergent for all sufficiently small extrapolation θ ≥ 0, so any universal sufficient condition κ < c(θ) has limsup c(θ) ≤ 2 as θ ↓ 0, below the quadratic bound 4/(1+2θ). A nonconstant three-cycle exists exactly when κ²(1+θ)² − 2κ(1+3θ) − 3 ≥ 0, and a rational seven-cycle has an open set of nonconvergent starts. The obstructing θ-intervals are very small.
families.formal_scope: The universal three-cycle threshold and its attainment, the seven-cycle with its open basin, the four-dimensional family for every κ > 2 and the quadratic eigenmode comparison are formalized in 21 Lean modules. The limsup consequence, numerical observations of larger θ-intervals and basin sizes, and the finite-dimensional matrix-convergence bridge are conventional or observational.
families.source: Banert, Upadhyaya and Giselsson proved convergence for θ > 1/2 and κ < 4/(1+2θ), and Upadhyaya gave a sufficient condition for small θ. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: The exact last-gradient bound for constant-step gradient descent in the strongly convex case
families.summary: The exact final-gradient guarantee holds on every real Hilbert space for L > 0, 0 ≤ μ ≤ L, normalized step 0 ≤ h ≤ 2 and every natural horizon. Actual one-dimensional Huber and quadratic functions attain its two branches.
families.formal_scope: The actual-function upper bound and normalized actual-function attainment are formalized, including every horizon and closed parameter boundary. Sharpness for arbitrary L > 0 and radius R > 0 is proved by rescaling in the manuscript, without a separate Lean wrapper.
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.source: Prior results and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Critical hard-core influence bounds via nonbacktracking collisions
families.kind: Theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: For every Δ ≥ 3, every n-vertex graph of maximum degree at most Δ, every hard-core activity 0 < λ ≤ λ_c(Δ) = (Δ−1)^(Δ−1)/(Δ−2)^Δ and every feasible pinning, each absolute row sum of the influence matrix is at most 1 + 12Δ(Δ−1)[λ/(1+λ)] r⌈log_{Δ−1} r⌉ with r = ⌊√(2Δn)⌋ + 1, an O_Δ(√n log n) ℓ∞-spectral-independence bound at the uniqueness threshold. The constant is large, and the Glauber-dynamics mixing consequence depends on a published proposition that is not formalized.
families.formal_scope: The influence bound for the actual hard-core Gibbs measure on every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most Δ, all activities up to λ_c(Δ) and all feasible pinnings is formalized in 32 Lean modules, including the regular completion and the nonbacktracking collision estimate. The Glauber-dynamics mixing corollary and the numerical observations on the constant are not formalized.
families.source: Chen and Jiang stated an O(√n) critical bound in 2025 and withdrew it in January 2026; Bencs et al. (2026) asked the critical two-spin question. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Counterexamples to a best-of-n win-rate bound at every budget
families.kind: Disproof for every budget n≥2 and every positive atom cap
families.summary: For every n≥2 and δ>0, there is a finite positive reference distribution whose largest atom is at most δ and whose best-of-n policy violates the proposed divergence–win-rate curve. A four-response best-of-two example gives exact probabilities and a strict logarithmic certificate. The proof uses finite interval bounds and gives a quantitative positive gap. It does not determine the sharp replacement curve.
families.source: Beirami et al., ICML 2025, Conjecture 7.2 and equation (28).

families.title: Logarithmic influence bounds and variance counterexamples for Boolean decision-tree covariance
families.kind: Finite covariance bounds and variance counterexamples
families.summary: For finite Boolean decision trees with no repeated coordinate on a root-to-leaf path, a logarithmic influence bound controls signed and absolute tree covariance. A known family attains equality at powers of two. Exact read-3 examples disprove the proposed coefficient-one variance replacement, including an example in which every query is relevant. No Fourier entropy theorem is formalized.
families.source: Wan, Wright, and Wu, ITCS 2014, Section 2.4; Shalev, arXiv:1806.03646v2, Section 6.2.

families.title: Ordered-instance allocation transfer with exact extra-copy preservation
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: A set-valued ordered-instance transfer preserving utility improvement, the exact extra-copy count, per-good caps and coverage.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The transfer theorem is formalized. Existence of a fair allocation before transfer is outside the result; external source comparison is provisional.

families.title: Unbounded coalesced-mass certificates for resolution trees
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: A coalesced dyadic clause-mass functional has exact supremum n+1 on the stated unrestricted resolution-tree class and is unbounded across dimensions.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The internally defined resolution-tree functional and proof class are formalized. No unconditional identification with an external conjecture or a regular proof class is claimed.

families.title: A three-state thermal counterexample to a heat-current kurtosis conjecture
families.kind: Exact finite spectral counterexample
families.summary: A three-state two-temperature thermal rate model satisfies local detailed balance and has an exact negative fourth-to-second cold-heat spectral cumulant ratio. Lean checks the finite matrices, complex spectrum, a smooth locally dominant eigenvalue branch, and the exact derivative ratio. It does not formalize the stochastic long-time identification theorem.
families.source: Ptaszyński, Physical Review E 106, 024119 (2022), Eq. (19).

families.title: A sharp universal skewness bound for unicyclic currents
families.summary: The net marked-edge current on every finite bidirectional Markov ring with at least three states, positive rates and unequal forward and reverse rate products satisfies −1/16 ≤ C₃/C₁ ≤ 1. The two-channel two-state case has the stronger interval [1/4,1]. This ratio is not standardized skewness.
families.formal_scope: The interval for actual tilted-matrix derivatives and a local branch is formalized. Identification with long-time stochastic cumulants and sharpness have conventional proofs. Lean does not construct a continuous-time sample-path probability space or a separate optimizing-sequence theorem.
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.source: Prior results and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Universal entanglement embezzlement with inverse-quadratic logarithmic infidelity
families.kind: Universal catalyst with a quantitative error bound
families.summary: A target-independent catalyst with local dimension 2^(4L) gives root infidelity at most 125m/L² for every Schmidt probability vector on m entries.
families.source: Van Dam and Hayden, 2003; Leung and Wang, 2014.
families.formal_scope: The proof constructs local basis permutations and establishes their finite complex Hilbert-space interpretation. Arbitrary changes to an external Schmidt basis are not separately formalized.

families.title: A sum-of-squares proof of the four-qubit Higuchi–Sudbery entropy bound
families.kind: Four-qubit entropy bound with attainment
families.summary: The average von Neumann entropy of the three two-qubit marginals of a pure four-qubit state is at most log(2) + log(3)/2. The Higuchi–Sudbery state attains this bound.
families.source: Higuchi and Sudbery, 2000. The Omega Institute publicly registered this problem on 5 October 2026 and committed a claimed Lean proof on 7 October 2026, with an algebraically equivalent sum-of-squares certificate; I make no originality or priority claim. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.
families.formal_scope: The proof uses all sixteen complex amplitudes, actual reduced-matrix eigenvalues, an exact sum-of-squares identity, and an explicit maximizing state.

families.title: A pure-state matched-basis information inequality violation in dimension five
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.summary: A dimension-five pure-state matched-basis information inequality violation, with a conventional all-prime companion.
families.source: Related work and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.
families.formal_scope: The dimension-five identical-local-basis theorem is formalized. The prime-family extension is conventional; arbitrary or independently optimized basis choices are outside the result.

families.title: Exact three-setting correlation bounds at fixed steering centre
families.summary: The exact least upper bound of the optimized three-setting squared correlation value is determined for every two-qubit steering-centre length. The threshold for a value greater than one is c < 2/3. Attainment, nonattainment and the singular marginal boundary are included.
families.formal_scope: Actual two-qubit density matrices, canonical filters, Pauli correlations, the exact least upper bound, attainment and nonattainment, and fully entangled fraction are formalized. The steering-ellipsoid and optimized CJWR measurement interpretations use cited external correspondences; general steerability is outside the result.
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.source: Prior results and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: The three-state root-fidelity entropy bound
families.summary: The entropy of the weighted three-by-three root-fidelity matrix bounds the Holevo quantity of every three-state ensemble in arbitrary finite dimension. The result includes mixed and singular states and zero probabilities.
families.formal_scope: The unrestricted three-state ensemble theorem is formalized for actual positive semidefinite complex matrices of trace one, nonnegative weights summing to one, spectral entropy and nuclear-norm root fidelity. Credited QICLean foundations and prior-work adapters retain their attribution.
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.source: Prior results and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified. Another group has claimed a solution of the same conjecture using AI and Lean; the proofs have not been compared, and neither equivalence nor priority has been established. See PRIORITY_AND_NOVELTY.md.

families.title: Exact conditional contraction for Pauli channels and depolarization in every dimension
families.summary: The conditional hockey-stick contraction coefficient is determined exactly for every stochastic Pauli qubit channel and for depolarization throughout its physical parameter interval in every dimension. The formulas include all boundary cases and every hockey-stick parameter γ ≥ 1, with arbitrary finite quantum references.
families.formal_scope: The exact conditional hockey-stick contraction coefficients are formalized for actual finite-reference density states, every stochastic Pauli qubit channel, the full physical signed depolarizing family in every dimension d ≥ 2, and every γ ≥ 1. Channel constructors, unrestricted upper bounds and matching supremum witnesses are included. Unital-qubit normal-form existence is cited; erasure-simulation and ensemble-guessing consequences retain conventional proofs.
families.kind: Standalone theorem and reproducible proof package
families.source: Prior results and source-comparison limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

families.title: Strong minimum-rank multiplicativity from unextendible product constraints
families.kind: Theorem, exact all-copy formula and reproducible proof package
families.summary: If a complex matrix subspace S is annihilated by an unextendible family of product functionals, every nonzero member of S ⊗ T has rank at least twice the minimum rank of T; if S also contains a rank-two matrix, m(S ⊗ T) = 2m(T) for every nonzero T. For the Tiles bound entangled state ρ, the Schmidt number of ρ^⊗N and the minimum rank of its support are exactly 2^N for every N ≥ 1.
families.formal_scope: The rank-doubling theorem with an arbitrary partner, strong minimum-rank multiplicativity, the Tiles support and normalized density operators, and the exact all-copy Schmidt-number equivalence are formalized in 22 Lean modules. The zero-error LOCC cost, the rank-four two-qutrit PPT class and the channel interpretation combine the formal theorem with published results.
families.source: The Tiles UPB is due to Bennett et al. (1999); Chen, Yang and Tang (2017) proved the two-copy case and Vidal and Cirac (2001) implied nonsharp exponential growth. Related work and limits are stated in the manuscript. Historical priority is not certified.

research_notes.status: The four-block and permutation-polynomial theorems have complete Lean proofs. The written proofs and exact certificates remain available. No first-priority or independent human expert review claim is made.
